newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Port Arthur gunman attempts suicide - radio.
newsitem.headline: Port Arthur gunman attempts suicide - radio.

text.p: Port Arthur gunman Martin Bryant has tried to end his life with an overdose of pills, Australian radio reported on Monday, the first anniversary of his shooting spree which killed 35 people.

Bryant, 29, was found in his prison cell about two weeks ago suffering the effects of an overdose of medication and with a makeshift noose, made from torn sheets, lying among his bedding, the Australian Broadcasting Corp reported.
The pills were supplied to him by another inmate at Risdon prison in Hobart, capital of the island state of Tasmania where the massacre took place, the unsourced radio report said.
"Noticing Bryant acting suspiciously he (a prison warder) entered his cell and found him to be groggy," it said.
News of the reported suicide attempt, the third time Bryant has tried to harm himself in prison, comes as Australians recall their country's worst massacre in modern times.
The focus of Monday's remembrances will be a memorial service held in the ruins of a stone church at Port Arthur, the former penal colony where Bryant opened fire on tourists on April 28 last year.
Hundreds of people, including survivors and relatives of the dead, are expected to attend.
Bryant is reported to have attempted suicide twice before, although prison authorities have declined to call them real attempts to end his own life.

Last month, Bryant was caught trying to swallow a rolled-up toothpaste tube but prison staff removed the tube from his mouth before he could injure himself. Last year, Bryant was found in his cell wrapping a bandage around his neck.

Jailed for life without parole last November, Bryant has been confined to the jail's hospital wing where he is kept mainly isolated in a suicide-proof cell monitored around the clock by video surveillance.
In recent months, the prison has allowed him to mix with other inmates in the hospital wing. Authorities ultimately want to introduce Bryant to the general prison population.
